mainTopic: How much of the סימנים must be cut for a valid שחיטה, and the source that שחיטה is done at the neck
overview: The משנה teaches how much of the windpipe and food pipe (the סימנים) must be cut for a kosher שחיטה: one סימן in a bird, two in an animal, and most of a סימן counts like all of it. רבי יהודה adds that the ורידין (neck veins) must also be cut. The גמרא reads the word השוחט as a בדיעבד ruling, and explains that this applies only to one סימן in a bird or to cutting a majority. Then three sources try to show from a פסוק that שחיטה is done at the neck: רב כהנא (ושחט, 'where it bends, purify it'), רב יימר (וזבחת, 'where it flows, cut it'), and דבי רבי ישמעאל (וסחט, 'where it speaks, purify it'). Each one is challenged with other body parts. Each time the גמרא concludes that the neck rule is a tradition, like the five disqualifications of שחיטה. The פסוק instead teaches not to cut the head off completely. Finally, a תנא brings רבי חייא's ברייתא. It calls the head of an עולה 'already cut off' at slaughter, which proves the cut is at the neck. The גמרא then sorts out which פסוק teaches including the head, and which teaches that the head and fat go on the מזבח first.

steps.title: The basic rule: one סימן in a bird, two in an animal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that cutting one סימן in a bird or two in an animal makes the שחיטה valid, and most of a סימן counts like the whole סימן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone slaughters by cutting one סימן in a bird and two in an animal, the שחיטה is kosher. Cutting most of one סימן counts like cutting all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens the chapter by stating the minimum cut needed for a kosher שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird needs only one of its two סימנים cut, while an animal needs both. The משנה adds that cutting רוב (the majority) of a סימן is treated just like cutting the whole thing.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the two pipes cut in שחיטה: the windpipe (קנה) or the food pipe (ושט)
The majority counts like the whole

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic halachic measure for every kosher שחיטה.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who slaughters by cutting one in a bird
phrases.notes: 'One' means one סימן, either the windpipe or the food pipe.

phrases.english: and two in an animal – his slaughter is valid,
and the majority of one is like it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶחָד בָּעוֹף וּשְׁנַיִם בַּבְּהֵמָה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One סימן in a bird and two in an animal make a valid שחיטה; most of a סימן equals the whole.

steps.title: רבי יהודה requires cutting the veins
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the שחיטה is not valid until the ורידין (major neck blood vessels) are also cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the שחיטה is not valid until he cuts the ורידין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion and adds another requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion only requires the סימנים. רבי יהודה adds that the ורידין must be cut too.

keyTerms.meaning: The large blood vessels in the neck
Not until; sets a condition that must be met

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Not until he cuts the veins.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁחוֹט אֶת הַוְּורִידִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the first opinion by adding a requirement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the ורידין must also be cut.

steps.title: Half is not enough, a majority is
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains the measure: half a סימן in a bird or one and a half in an animal is invalid, but a majority is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Half of one סימן in a bird, or one and a half in an animal, makes the שחיטה invalid. Most of one in a bird, or most of both in an animal, makes it valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה spells out where the line falls between a valid and an invalid cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Exactly half does not count as a majority, so it fails. Even in an animal, cutting one and a half fails, because the second סימן is only half cut. Once each needed סימן is more than half cut, the שחיטה works.

keyTerms.meaning: Invalid; the animal is not kosher

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think one and a half סימנים in an animal is 'more than one' and so good enough. Each סימן needed must be mostly cut.
steps.whatToRemember: Bird: most of one סימן. Animal: most of both סימנים. Exactly half is never enough.

phrases.english: Half of one in a bird
or one and a half in an animal – his slaughter is invalid.
The majority of one in a bird
or the majority of two in an animal – his slaughter is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲצִי אֶחָד בְּעוֹף וְאֶחָד וָחֵצִי בִּבְהֵמָה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Half is invalid; a majority is valid.

steps.title: The word השוחט implies after-the-fact only
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the word השוחט as a hint that the ruling is only בדיעבד, not לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who slaughters' means: after the fact, yes, it is valid; from the start, no, one should not do it this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from how the משנה is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'one who slaughtered' describes something already done. That suggests the משנה approves the result בדיעבד but does not allow it לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
From the start; the ideal way

phrases.english: GEMARA: "One who slaughters"
after the fact, yes; from the start, no.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's ruling is בדיעבד only.

steps.title: But an animal only has two סימנים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the inference: if two סימנים in an animal is only בדיעבד, what more could one cut לכתחילה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Two in an animal is not allowed from the start? How much more should he keep cutting?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the inference from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal has only two סימנים, so cutting both is the most anyone can do. It makes no sense to call that 'only בדיעבד.'

phrases.english: Two in an animal – from the start, no?
How far should he slaughter and keep going?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the בדיעבד inference.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the whole משנה is only בדיעבד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cutting both סימנים in an animal is the maximum possible, so it can't be merely בדיעבד.

steps.title: The בדיעבד part refers to a bird or to 'majority'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the בדיעבד inference applies only to one סימן in a bird, or only to cutting a majority of a סימן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it refers to one in a bird. Or if you want, say it refers to 'the majority of one is like it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two possible answers that limit which part of the משנה is בדיעבד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First answer: in a bird one should cut both סימנים לכתחילה, so one is only בדיעבד. Second answer: one should cut each סימן fully לכתחילה, so a majority is only בדיעבד. Either way, cutting two in an animal stays fine.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say; introduces a possible answer

phrases.english: If you want, say: it refers to one in a bird,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: אַרוּבּוֹ שֶׁל אֶחָד כָּמוֹהוּ.
phrases.english: and if you want, say: it refers to 'the majority of one is like it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the inference to one part of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה, including two in an animal, is בדיעבד.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one סימן in a bird, or a majority of a סימן, is בדיעבד.
steps.whatToRemember: Ideally one cuts both סימנים fully. The משנה's smaller amounts work only after the fact.

steps.title: Memory aid for the coming statements
steps.stepSummary: A short memory aid lists the speakers of the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: A memory aid: כ, מ, ש.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. It gives a memory aid for the statements the גמרא is about to bring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters stand for רב כהנא, רב יימר, and דבי רבי ישמעאל, whose statements follow in order.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a memory aid, not a pipe in the neck

phrases.english: (Kaf, Mem, Shin – a memory aid).
phrases.notes: The letters hint at רב כהנא, רב יימר, and the school of רבי ישמעאל, who are quoted next.

steps.title: רב כהנא: שחיטה is at the neck
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא learns from the word ושחט that שחיטה is done where the animal bends, at the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: How do we know שחיטה is done at the neck? The פסוק says 'ושחט the young bull,' meaning: from the place where it bends (שח), purify it (חטהו).
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives a source from a פסוק for where on the animal שחיטה is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He splits the word ושחט into two parts: שח (bends) and חט (purify). The neck is the place where an animal bends, so that is where it is 'purified' through שחיטה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the תורה source for the neck being the place of שחיטה.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
From where do we know that slaughter is from the neck?
As it says: "And he shall slaughter the young bull,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:5

phrases.english: from the place where it bends, purify it.
phrases.notes: He reads ושחט as two words joined: שח (bends) and חט (purify).

steps.mimraCoreRuling: שחיטה is done at the neck, learned from ושחט read as 'where it bends, purify it.'

steps.title: How do we know חטהו means purify?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for proof that חטהו is a word meaning purification.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that this word חטהו means purifying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רב כהנא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא's whole reading depends on חט meaning 'purify.' The גמרא wants proof that the word really has that meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do we know?

phrases.english: From where do we know that this 'purify it'
is a term of purifying?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי דְּהַאי חַטֵּהוּ לִישָּׁנָא דְּדַכּוֹיֵי הוּא

steps.title: Two פסוקים prove חטא means purify
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings two פסוקים where a form of חטא means to purify.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And he shall purify the house.' Or if you want, from here: 'Purify me with hyssop and I will be pure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with proof from פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ויקרא, וחטא is used for purifying a house with צרעת. In תהלים, תחטאני is paired with ואטהר ('I will be pure'), which clearly shows the meaning. So חטהו can mean purify.

keyTerms.meaning: Hyssop, a plant used in purification

steps.whatToRemember: שחיטה is done at the neck: ושחט means 'where it bends (שח), purify it (חט).' חטא can mean purify, as proven from two פסוקים.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And he shall purify the house,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:52

phrases.english: and if you want, say it is learned from here:
"Purify me with hyssop and I will be pure."
phrases.notes: תהלים 51:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the meaning of חטהו.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: וחטא את הבית (ויקרא) or תחטאני באזוב ואטהר (תהלים) show that חטא means purify.

steps.title: Why not slaughter from the tail?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב כהנא: the tail also bends, so maybe שחיטה should be done there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that it should be done from its tail!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes at רב כהנא's reading. If שחיטה goes where the animal bends, the tail bends too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא read ושחט as 'where it bends (שח), purify it (חטהו).' The גמרא asks why that points to the neck and not to the tail, which is also a bent part of the body.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But say...': a way of suggesting a different possibility to challenge an idea

phrases.english: But say: from its tail?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב כהנא's derivation from step 8, now that the meaning of חטהו is settled.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's reading of ושחט as 'where it bends'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The tail is also a bending part, so the derivation does not single out the neck.

steps.title: The tail is always bent, never upright
steps.stepSummary: The word שח implies a part that can stand upright and then bend. The tail is permanently bent.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Bends' implies that we need something that is upright. But the tail is bent all the time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'bending' only makes sense for something that is normally upright. The tail never is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only say something 'bends' if it can also stand up straight. The neck rises and lowers, but the tail just hangs down all the time. So the word שח excludes the tail.

keyTerms.meaning: by implication, from the meaning of

phrases.english: 'Bends': this implies that we need something upright,
and this one stays bent all the time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the tail challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refining the meaning of the word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any bending body part could qualify, including the tail.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a part that can be upright and then bend qualifies, which excludes the tail.

steps.title: Why not slaughter from the ear?
steps.stepSummary: The ear stands upright and bends, so maybe שחיטה should be done there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that it should be done from its ear!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again. The ear fits the new rule, since it is upright and can bend.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer required a part that is upright and bends. The ear meets that test, so the challenge returns.

phrases.english: But say: from its ear?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge built on the refined rule from step 12.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ear meets that criterion, so the neck is still not singled out.

steps.title: The ear has no life-blood
steps.stepSummary: שחיטה must release דם הנפש, and cutting the ear does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need the blood of life, and there is none there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שחיטה has to be at a spot where cutting spills the life-blood. The ear is not such a spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A second requirement is added. Besides bending, the place of שחיטה must release דם הנפש, the blood that ends the animal's life. The ear fails this test.

keyTerms.meaning: life-blood: the blood whose loss kills the animal

phrases.english: We need the blood of life, and there isn't any.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ear challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any upright, bending part qualifies, including the ear.
steps.terutzMaskana: The place must also release דם הנפש, which excludes the ear.

steps.title: Why not cut from the ear down to the life-blood? And where do the disqualifications come from?
steps.stepSummary: Maybe one could start at the ear and keep cutting until reaching דם הנפש. Also, the five disqualifications of שחיטה have no פסוק either.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that he tears and keeps going until he reaches the blood of life! And furthermore: pausing, pressing, covering, slipping out of place, and ripping out — where do we learn these from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a double attack. First, the ear could still work if you keep cutting down to the blood. Second, the well-known rules that ruin a שחיטה also have no פסוק, so why expect one here?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The דם הנפש answer is not enough: start at the ear and continue to the blood vessels. Then the גמרא widens the question. The five things that make a שחיטה invalid have no clear source in a פסוק, which suggests the details of שחיטה come from somewhere other than פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: pausing in the middle of the cut
pressing the knife down instead of drawing it
hiding the knife under the skin or סימנים while cutting
cutting outside the proper area of the neck
ripping the סימנים out of place

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵימָא: דְּקָרַע וְאָזֵיל עַד דַּם הַנֶּפֶשׁ!
phrases.english: But say: he tears and keeps going until he reaches the blood of life!
And furthermore: pausing, pressing, covering,
slipping out of place, and ripping out: where do we learn these from?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: דְּקָרַע וְאָזֵיל עַד דַּם הַנֶּפֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 14 and questions the whole approach of deriving שחיטה rules from פסוקים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The attempt to locate שחיטה at the neck from the פסוק ושחט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cutting from the ear down to the blood would meet every stated requirement. Also, the other basic rules of שחיטה have no פסוק source, so the פסוק-based approach is not convincing.

steps.title: Slaughter at the neck is a received tradition
steps.stepSummary: Just like the five disqualifications, the rule that שחיטה is done at the neck comes from tradition, not from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a tradition. Slaughter from the neck is also a tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on deriving the neck rule from ושחט. It concludes that the rule, like the five disqualifications, was handed down as a tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the disqualifications clearly come from a received tradition, the location of the cut does too. רב כהנא's word-play is not the real source.

keyTerms.meaning: here: a received tradition handed down (in the sense of הלכה למשה מסיני), not the name of the Talmud

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word גמרא does not mean 'the Talmud.' It means a tradition that was learned and handed down.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule that שחיטה is done at the neck, and the five disqualifications of שחיטה, all come from received tradition (גמרא), not from a פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the basic laws of שחיטה rest on oral tradition. That is why the פסוק has to be explained as teaching something else.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a tradition.
Slaughter from the neck is also a tradition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the force of step 15 and changes the source of the rule from a פסוק to tradition.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שחיטה at the neck is known by tradition, like שהייה, דרסה, חלדה, הגרמה, and עיקור.

steps.title: Then what does the פסוק teach?
steps.stepSummary: If the neck rule comes from tradition, the גמרא asks what the פסוק ושחט comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the פסוק, what does it come for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks what job the פסוק does now that it isn't the source for the neck rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes a פסוק must teach something. Since the location now comes from tradition, it needs another purpose for the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: what does it come to teach?

phrases.english: And the פסוק, what does it come for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the conclusion in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of the פסוק ושחט if the neck rule comes from tradition.

steps.title: Don't cut the head off completely
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק teaches that one should not chop the animal into a broken piece by cutting off its whole head.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that he should not make it into a broken thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק teaches not to cut through the whole neck. You only cut the windpipe and food pipe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the location of the cut now comes from tradition, the פסוק ושחט is free for a different lesson. It teaches how much to cut, not where: cut the סימנים, but do not sever the whole head.

phrases.english: So that he should not make it into a broken thing.
phrases.notes: Don't cut the head off completely and leave the animal like a broken piece.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches not to sever the head completely.

steps.title: רב יימר: 'Where it flows, cut it'
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר learns the neck rule from וזבחת, reading it as זב חתהו: 'where it flows, cut it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר said: The פסוק says 'And you shall slaughter': from the place where it flows, cut it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר gives a different source for the neck rule. He splits the word וזבחת into 'flows' (זב) and 'cut it' (חתהו).
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a second word-play, separate from רב כהנא's ושחט. It points to the place where the blood flows, which is the neck.

phrases.english: רב יימר said: The פסוק says 'And you shall slaughter,'
phrases.notes: דברים 12:21

phrases.english: from the place where it flows, cut it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different derivation of the neck rule, in place of רב כהנא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שחיטה is done at the place where the blood flows, learned from וזבחת = זב חתהו.

steps.title: How do we know חתהו means breaking?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for proof that the word חתהו means breaking.
steps.simpleTranslation: What shows that this word חתהו is a word for breaking?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof that the second half of רב יימר's word-play really means 'break it.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יימר's derivation only works if חת means cutting or breaking. This question is like the one asked about חטהו in step 9.

phrases.english: What shows that this word חתהו
is a word for breaking?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי חַתֵּהוּ לִישָּׁנָא דְּמִתְבַּר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the word meaning in רב יימר's derivation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that חת means breaking.

steps.title: Proof from 'ואל תחת'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'Do not fear and do not be broken (תחת)' shows that חת means breaking.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Do not fear and do not be broken.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק where the root חת means being broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In 'ואל תחת' the word means don't let your spirit be broken. That shows חת means breaking, so חתהו means 'break it,' and רב יימר's reading holds.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two word-play sources for שחיטה at the neck: רב כהנא's ושחט and רב יימר's וזבחת. The גמרא's main conclusion is that the neck rule is a received tradition.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'Do not fear and do not be broken.'
phrases.notes: דברים 1:21

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The root חת means breaking, as in 'ואל תחת'.

steps.title: Why not slaughter from the nose?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יימר: something flows from the nose too, so maybe one should cut there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And say that one slaughters from its nose!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב יימר's reading 'where it flows, cut it'. The nose also has something flowing from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק as read by רב יימר only says 'where it flows' and never mentions blood. Mucus flows from the nose, so the derivation seems to point to the nose just as much as the neck.

keyTerms.meaning: And say instead (a challenge offering another possibility)

phrases.english: And say [one slaughters] from its nose,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the scope of רב יימר's derivation from וזבחת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The nose also has a flow, so 'where it flows' does not pick out the neck.

steps.title: The flow must come from cutting
steps.stepSummary: The answer: we need a flow caused by cutting, and mucus flows by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need something that flows through cutting, and this flows on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the nose challenge. The פסוק means a flow that comes from the cut itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זב חתהו' is read as one connected idea: the cutting makes the flow. Mucus comes out of the nose without any cut, so the nose does not fit the reading.

phrases.english: We need [something that] flows by means of cutting,
and this flows on its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב יימר against the nose challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the reading of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any place that has a flow would qualify.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a flow produced by the cut counts.

steps.title: Why not the heart, and where do the other rules come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: stabbing the heart also makes blood flow through a cut. Besides, the five disqualifications of שחיטה have no פסוק at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And say from its heart! And furthermore: interrupting, pressing, covering, slipping out of place, and ripping — where do we know them from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger challenge. A stab to the heart does produce a flow through cutting. It then adds a second point: many rules of שחיטה have no source in a פסוק at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heart passes the test from Step 23, so 'זב חתהו' still does not pick out the neck. The five disqualifications (שהייה, דרסה, חלדה, הגרמה, עיקור) are not written in the תורה, which hints that the laws of שחיטה come from a different kind of source.

keyTerms.meaning: Pausing in the middle of the cut
Pressing the knife down instead of drawing it
Hiding the knife under the skin or the pipes
Cutting outside the proper area of the neck
Tearing the pipes out instead of cutting them

steps.confusionAlert: The list of five is not a new topic. It is proof that much of שחיטה is known without a פסוק.

phrases.english: And say [one slaughters] from its heart,
and furthermore: interrupting, pressing, covering,
diverting, and ripping — from where do we [know them]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Escalates the challenge after the nose was ruled out.
steps.kashyaTarget: Deriving the neck rule from 'זב חתהו'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The heart also has a flow through cutting. And the five disqualifications have no פסוק, so a פסוק is not needed for everything about שחיטה.

steps.title: The neck rule is a tradition
steps.stepSummary: Conclusion: just like the five disqualifications, cutting at the neck is known by tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a tradition. Slaughtering from the neck is also a tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the neck rule is not really learned from the פסוק. It is a received tradition, just like the five disqualifications.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The five disqualifications are known from tradition, and the neck rule sits alongside them. This drops the need for רב יימר's derivation and leads straight to the next question: what does the פסוק teach, then?

keyTerms.meaning: Received tradition (here, not the name of the Talmud)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'גמרא' means a tradition handed down, not the Talmud text you are learning.

phrases.english: Rather, [they are known by] tradition.
Slaughter from the neck is also [known by] tradition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the heart challenge and the list of five.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Cutting at the neck is a tradition, not learned from וזבחת.

steps.title: Then what is the פסוק for?
steps.stepSummary: If the neck rule is a tradition, the גמרא asks what the פסוק וזבחת comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the פסוק, what does it come for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. If tradition gives us the neck rule, the פסוק must be teaching something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes a פסוק is never extra. Now that the neck rule needs no פסוק, the פסוק's own lesson must be found.

keyTerms.meaning: For what does it come? (What does it teach?)

phrases.english: And the verse, for what does it come?
phrases.notes: This is the same question as Step 17, now asked about רב יימר's פסוק, וזבחת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the conclusion that the neck rule is a tradition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the פסוק וזבחת teaches.

steps.title: Do not make it a broken piece
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק teaches not to cut off the whole head and turn the animal into a broken piece.
steps.simpleTranslation: That one should not make it a broken piece.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the פסוק teaches that one should not cut all the way through the head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'חתהו' (break it) is now read as a limit on the cut, not as the source for where to cut. One cuts the windpipe and gullet without chopping off the whole head.

keyTerms.meaning: A broken piece / a shattered thing

phrases.english: That one should not make it a broken piece.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק forbids severing the head completely.
steps.whatToRemember: With רב יימר's derivation, as with the first one, the neck rule ends up as tradition, and the פסוק teaches not to chop off the head.

steps.title: Where it speaks, cut it
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל reads ושחט as וסחט: cut the animal at the place it 'speaks', which is the throat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'And he shall slaughter' — do not read ושחט but וסחט: from the place where it speaks, purify it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new source for the neck rule is brought. דבי רבי ישמעאל reads the word ושחט in a new way that points to the throat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swapping ש for ס turns ושחט into 'סח חטהו': where it speaks (סח), purify it (חטהו). An animal's voice comes from its throat, so this points to the neck.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read (a re-reading of a word to learn something)

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
'And he shall slaughter' — do not read 'veshachat,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:5

phrases.english: but rather 'vesachat,'
from the place where it speaks, purify it.
phrases.notes: The animal's sound comes from its throat, so this means the neck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק-based source for the neck rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The neck rule comes from reading ושחט as 'סח חטהו'.

steps.title: Why not the tongue?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: speech also involves the tongue, so maybe one should cut there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And say from its tongue!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests דבי רבי ישמעאל the same way it tested רב כהנא, who was asked about the ear. The tongue is also a 'place of speaking'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The place where it speaks' could just as well mean the tongue as the throat. So the reading does not clearly point to the neck.

phrases.english: And say [one slaughters] from its tongue!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new derivation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The tongue is also a place of speech.

steps.title: We need lifeblood
steps.stepSummary: The answer: שחיטה must release the lifeblood, and cutting the tongue does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need the blood of the soul, and there is none.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the tongue challenge. The cut must release the main lifeblood, and the tongue does not have it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An added requirement, דם הנפש, narrows the reading down to the throat. Cutting the tongue does not spill the blood that the animal's life depends on.

keyTerms.meaning: Lifeblood, the blood the animal's life depends on

phrases.english: We need blood of the soul, and there is none [in the tongue],

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the derivation against the tongue challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a requirement that rules out the tongue
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any place of speech would qualify.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a place where cutting releases lifeblood qualifies.

steps.title: Start at the tongue and tear onward
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: one could start at the tongue and keep tearing until lifeblood comes. Again, the five disqualifications have no פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And say that he tears and continues until the blood of the soul! And furthermore, interrupting, pressing, covering, diverting, and ripping — where do we know them from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes past the answer. One could begin cutting at the tongue and continue until reaching lifeblood. It repeats the point about the five disqualifications.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lifeblood requirement can be met even if the cut begins at the tongue. So the reading still does not force cutting at the neck itself, and the five rules again show that tradition is the real source.

phrases.english: And say that he tears and continues
until the blood of the soul!
And furthermore, interrupting, pressing, covering,
diverting, and ripping — from where do we [know them]?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא דְּקָרַע וְאָזֵיל עַד דַּם הַנֶּפֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Escalates the challenge against the lifeblood answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The lifeblood answer and the וסחט derivation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lifeblood can be reached starting from the tongue, and the five disqualifications show the rules are not from פסוקים.

steps.title: Again, the neck rule is a tradition
steps.stepSummary: As before, the conclusion is that the neck rule, like the five disqualifications, is a tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a tradition. Slaughtering from the neck is also a tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the same conclusion it reached about רב יימר. The neck rule is known by tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא repeats the same words as Step 25 on purpose, because the same reasoning knocks out דבי רבי ישמעאל's source too. Every attempted פסוק source ends up showing that the neck rule is a tradition.
steps.whatToRemember: Each attempted source for cutting at the neck (ושחט, וזבחת, וסחט) is tested and fails. The rule stands as a tradition, alongside שהייה, דרסה, חלדה, הגרמה and עיקור.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the basic method of שחיטה rests on a received tradition, not on reading פסוקים.

phrases.english: Rather, [they are known by] tradition;
slaughter from the neck is also [known by] tradition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא גְּמָרָא, שְׁחִיטָה מִן הַצַּוָּאר נָמֵי גְּמָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the challenge to דבי רבי ישמעאל.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Cutting at the neck is a tradition, not learned from וסחט.

steps.title: What does the word ושחט teach, then?
steps.stepSummary: If the neck rule is a tradition, the גמרא asks what the פסוק of ושחט comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the verse, what does it come for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just said the neck rule is a tradition. So now it asks what job the פסוק of ושחט still has. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, דבי רבי ישמעאל used ושחט to find the place of cutting. Once the גמרא decided the neck rule is a tradition, that word seems to have no job left. The גמרא assumes every word in the תורה teaches something, so it asks what this one teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it come to teach?

phrases.english: And the verse, what does it come for?
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק ושחט that דבי רבי ישמעאל read as וסחט back in step 28.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the conclusion of step 32 that the neck rule is a tradition. That leaves the פסוק without an obvious job.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does ושחט teach, if not the place of the cut?

steps.title: Don't cut the head off completely
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק teaches that you must not cut the head all the way off and turn the animal into a 'broken piece'.
steps.simpleTranslation: That one should not make it a broken shard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ושחט teaches a limit. You cut the throat, but you do not chop off the whole head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא gives the same answer it gave for רב כהנא and רב יימר. The word ושחט is not the source for cutting at the neck, but it still has a job: it teaches that one should not cut the head off completely.

keyTerms.meaning: A broken shard, like a smashed piece of pottery

phrases.english: That one should not make it a broken shard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ושחט teaches that one may not cut off the whole head.

steps.title: A תנא brings a פסוק source through רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: A תנא does find a פסוק for the neck rule. He quotes a ברייתא in which רבי חייא learns it from 'And the sons of אהרן shall arrange the pieces'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a תנא brings it from here, as it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי חייא says, from where do we know that שחיטה is from the neck? As it says, 'And the sons of אהרן the כהנים shall arrange the pieces.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now offers a different view: a פסוק source for cutting at the neck. It names the פסוק here, and the next step explains how the proof works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא said the neck rule is only a tradition. This תנא disagrees and finds a source in the עולה פסוקים in ויקרא. The proof depends on the words that come right after 'the pieces': 'the head and the fat'.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, a reciter of משניות and ברייתות in the study hall
The cut-up pieces of the קרבן

phrases.english: And a tanna brings it from here,
As it is taught: Rabbi Chiyya says:
From where do we know that slaughter is from the neck?
As it says: "And the sons of Aaron shall arrange
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:8. The פסוק goes on to say 'the head and the fat', and that is the key to the proof.

phrases.english: the priests, the pieces."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a פסוק source, which disagrees with step 32's conclusion that the neck rule is only a tradition.
steps.raayaObject: That שחיטה must be done at the neck
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 1:8, 'And the sons of אהרן shall arrange the pieces'

steps.title: Why the head and fat are named separately
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא explains: the head and fat are already part of 'the pieces'. They are named separately because the head is cut off at slaughter, so it is not part of the flaying. It needs its own mention to be included.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse didn't need to say 'the head and the fat'. Why does it say them? Weren't they already part of all the pieces? Why were they singled out? Because it says 'He shall flay the עולה and cut it up'. From that I would only know about pieces that are part of the flaying. From where do we include the head, which was already cut off? The verse says 'its head and its fat, and he shall arrange'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא asks why the תורה names the head separately when it is already one of the pieces. He answers that the head is cut off before the flaying, so it needs a separate mention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flaying פסוק talks about pieces that get skinned and cut up. The head was already cut off at slaughter, so you might think it is left out of the arranging on the מזבח. So the תורה names the head on its own to include it. The key detail is that the head was already cut off at the time of slaughter.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse says / why does the verse need to say
The fat (covering the area of the slaughter)

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אֶת הָרֹאשׁ וְאֶת הַפָּדֶר״,
phrases.english: For there was no need for the verse to say "the head and the fat,"

phrases.aramaic: מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אֶת הָרֹאשׁ וְאֶת הַפָּדֶר״?
phrases.english: Why does the verse say "the head and the fat"?
Weren't the head and the fat
included among all the pieces,
why were they singled out?
Because it says: "And he shall flay the burnt offering and cut it up,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:6

phrases.english: I would only know about pieces
that are part of the flaying,
From where do we include the head
which was already cut off?
The verse says: "its head
and its fat, and he shall arrange."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:12

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֵין תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר אֶת הָרֹאשׁ וְאֶת הַפָּדֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק cited in step 35 works as a source.
steps.raayaObject: That the head is already cut off at slaughter
steps.raayaSupportSource: The separate mention of 'the head and the fat' in ויקרא 1:8 and 1:12, read against the flaying פסוק in ויקרא 1:6

steps.title: So the cut must be at the neck
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי חייא calls the head 'already cut off' at slaughter, we learn that שחיטה is done at the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the fact that he says 'the head which was already cut off', we learn that שחיטה is from the neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The תנא draws the conclusion from רבי חייא's words: the head is cut off at slaughter, so the cut must be at the neck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The head can only come off during slaughter if the cut is made at the neck, which joins the head to the body. So the תורה's wording assumes the slaughter is at the neck. That gives the neck rule a source in a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication, we learn from this

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on the neck rule. One says it is a tradition, and then ושחט teaches not to cut the head off completely. The other, a תנא citing רבי חייא, learns it from the עולה פסוקים: the head counts as 'already cut off' at slaughter, so the cut must be at the neck.

phrases.english: From the fact that he says "the head which was already cut off,"
we learn by implication that slaughter is from the neck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from רבי חייא's explanation in step 36.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to this תנא, the rule that שחיטה is at the neck comes from a פסוק: the head counts as already cut off at slaughter, which only happens if the cut is at the neck.

steps.title: The ברייתא starts with one פסוק and ends with another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the תנא of the ברייתא asks about "ראש ופדר" but finishes with "ראשו ופדרו", which is a different פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא opened by asking about the words "the head and the fat," but he ends by explaining "its head and its fat." That doesn't match!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רבי חייא's ברייתא: its question and its answer seem to talk about two different פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "The head and the fat" is written about a bull עולה, and "its head and its fat" is written about a sheep עולה. A ברייתא should explain the same words it asked about, so the switch looks like a mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of a ברייתא or משנה
The fat, used to cover the cut neck on the מזבח

phrases.english: And the tanna opened with "the head and the fat,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:8, about the bull עולה.

phrases.english: and he ends with "its head and its fat"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:12, about the sheep עולה. Notice the small change: "its" head.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא פָּתַח בְּ״רֹאשׁ וּפֶדֶר״, וּמְסַיֵּים בְּ״רֹאשׁוֹ וּפִדְרוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the wording of the ברייתא brought as proof in steps 35-36.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of רבי חייא's ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The question is about one פסוק and the answer quotes a different פסוק, so the two parts don't fit together.

steps.title: The already-cut head is learned from "the head and the fat"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא: the question and the answer are both about "את הראש ואת הפדר".
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the תנא means: How do we know to include the head that was already cut off? Because the פסוק says "the head and the fat."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what the ברייתא really means: the source for including the cut-off head is "the head and the fat".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question and the answer now match, because both use the bull פסוק (ויקרא 1:8). That leaves the sheep פסוק, "its head and its fat", without a job here, and this sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means. The גמרא is rereading a text

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
From where do we know to include the head
phrases.notes: Include it among the pieces placed on the מזבח.

phrases.english: which was already cut off?
The verse says: "the head and the fat."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 38.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא so its question and answer use the same פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to answer with "ראשו ופדרו", which doesn't match its question.
steps.terutzMaskana: The cut-off head is included by "את הראש ואת הפדר" (ויקרא 1:8).

steps.title: Then what is "its head and its fat" for?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the cut-off head comes from the bull פסוק, the גמרא asks why the sheep פסוק "ראשו ופדרו" is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need the words "its head and its fat"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the second פסוק teaches, since it is no longer the source for the cut-off head. It is setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה doesn't repeat words for no reason. Once "the head and the fat" covers the cut-off head, "its head and its fat" must teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? This asks what extra words teach

phrases.english: And why do I need "its head and its fat"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the answer in step 39, which left the second פסוק without a job.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the words "ראשו ופדרו" (ויקרא 1:12) come to teach

steps.title: "Its head and its fat" teaches that they go first
steps.stepSummary: "ראשו ופדרו" is needed for another ברייתא: the head and fat are placed on the מזבח before all the other pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what another ברייתא teaches: How do we know that the head and fat come before all the other pieces? Because the פסוק says "its head and its fat, and he shall arrange."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second פסוק teaches the order: the head and fat are offered on the מזבח first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now each פסוק has its own job. "The head and the fat" includes the cut-off head, and "its head and its fat, and he shall arrange" puts the head and fat first in line. The proof from step 37 still stands: שחיטה is done at the neck.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for, it is used to teach
The pieces of the animal offered on the מזבח
And he shall arrange (on the מזבח)

steps.whatToRemember: Two פסוקים, two jobs: "את הראש ואת הפדר" includes the head that was cut off at שחיטה, and "את ראשו ואת פדרו וערך" teaches that the head and fat go on the מזבח before the other pieces.

phrases.english: It is needed for what is taught in a baraita:
From where do we know that the head and the fat
come before all the other pieces?
The verse says:
"With its head and its fat, and he shall arrange."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 40.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "ראשו ופדרו" teaches that the head and fat are offered on the מזבח before all the other pieces.
